description: c's written [T [U s]] reads the synthetic T, so the item after T is strict, and it predicts the helper of [U s] strictly. That helper reads the synthetic U by route 3 too, and the item after U is strict, although a strict item read U. Nothing after s can read and s itself cannot, so s is not predicted there, and its tag term, which fails over an empty span, is never evaluated. [U s] is the restoration of U, the rest of [T [U s]] reads, and c is a second reading with V read as a bare terminal. A library that makes the item after U ordinary because the item that read it was strict evaluates s and fails with an error of the grammar. The empty rest must throw, since an empty rest that does not throw only adds a derivation to a reading that already competes (engine §7.4).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%elidable T U V W
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a A [T] [U] [V]
%rule b A [T] [U] [V] [W]
%rule c A [T [U s]] V
%rule s ε <tag(text($))>
